## Observed basis and remaining falsifiers

Observed source facts: accepted oracle `CORE/WRITE6` and `WRITE8` contain respectively one and two positive predicted targets; corrected target-a and target-b files show their bounded identifiers; held `CORE` source is `package definition\nfunc target() {}\n`; raw old definition frames use numeric IDs 141/142; B4a WRITE envelopes identify old owner keys, transaction/session and CAP/QUERY predecessor selectors; manager `roundTrip` uses `json.Marshal(lspwire.Message)` and allocates a numeric key; `sessionkey.Derive` has deterministic opaque profile identity. These establish a **derivation recipe**, not the as-yet-unauthored A/B originals.

Must still falsify at exact-byte review: predicted session IDs against profile material; newly authored request frames against the runtime writer's byte order; all new B4a/A4 and B4b CAP selectors/digests against independent original bytes; A/B source-range bounds; ability to produce both distinct exact response frames from a purpose-built future child while retaining manager ownership; and pre-write atomic owner binding before actual WRITE. No positive result is licensed while any remains unconfirmed. No tests, RED or Go source changes were made to obtain this derivation.
